newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli bonds rise ahead of rate announcement.
newsitem.headline: Israeli bonds rise ahead of rate announcement.

text.p: Israeli bonds closed slightly higher in dull trading on Sunday ahead of the Bank of Israel's interest rate announcement on Monday, traders said.
* Unlinked government bonds (Gilon -- issued for four years): +0.02 pct at 103.05
* Bank of Israel short-term Makam bills: +0.07 pct at 102.18
Volume was low at 112 million shekels with most of the trading concentrated in the Makams.

"The market continues to be very stable. Investors are waiting for the rate decision on Monday. The market expects a maximum rate cut of 0.3 percentage point (from the current 14.2 percent)," said Dan Lallouz, portfolio manager at Clal Insurance.
"Bond prices closed almost unchanged. Only a rate reduction of more than 0.5 percentage point will have a positive impact on the market," said another trader.
"CPI-linked bonds were mixed today with long bonds declining and short bonds rising. Overall the market is stable," said Gila Sukury of Israel Discount Bank.

"Yields on long-inflation-linked bonds fell sharply over the last few weeks to 4.1 percent. This happened too fast and yields are now rising. I believe that they will stabilise at 4.3 percent," Lallouz said.
He added that unlinked bonds, which rose slightly today, have reached an equilibrium.
"Volume in the Makam was relatively high today at 58 million shekels," Sukury added.
"Dollar-linked bonds closed lower today. They made a very big move (over the last two weeks) and today's decline might be a reaction to the overshooting in those bonds," she said.
Note: Makams are zero-coupon unlinked certificates with durations of three months to one year. The Bank of Israel issues Makams to absorb liquidity.
